core_obligations: Choose an affine scheme $U = \Spec(B)$ with a surjective etale morphism $\varphi : U \to X$, and note that $R = U \times_X U = \Spec(C)$ is affine because the situation is separated (proof lines 3171-3176).

Choose $g_1, \ldots, g_m \in B$ whose images under $s$ generate $C$ over $t : B \to C$, and show that the resulting map $\mathcal{O}_X[z_1, \ldots, z_n] \to \varphi_*\mathcal{O}_U$ becomes surjective after restricting to $U$, using the base change identification $\varphi^*\varphi_*\mathcal{O}_U = t_*\mathcal{O}_R$ (proof lines 3179-3192).

Apply the vanishing of $H^1$ to the kernel to conclude that $A[x_1, \ldots, x_n] \to B$ is surjective, so that $B$ is a finite type $A$-algebra and $X \to \Spec(A)$ is of finite type and separated (proof lines 3193-3200).

Deduce that $X \to \Spec(A)$ is locally quasi-finite, hence representable, so that $X$ is a scheme; then apply the affine criterion for quasi-compact schemes to obtain that $X$ is affine (proof lines 3201-3209).
proof_roadmap: The affine etale cover and its fibre product (proof lines 3171-3179).
Generators of $C$ and the presentation of $\varphi_*\mathcal{O}_U$ (proof lines 3179-3192).
Finite type of $B$ over $A$ from the vanishing of $H^1$ (proof lines 3193-3200).
$X$ is a separated locally quasi-finite scheme, hence affine (proof lines 3201-3209).
difficulty_reason: The proposition is Serre's criterion for affineness for quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces: affineness is equivalent to the vanishing of the higher cohomology of quasi-coherent sheaves (statement lines 3159-3168, with the slogan recording the classical name). The proof picks an affine etale cover, uses separatedness to make the fibre product affine, manufactures a finite presentation of the pushforward of the structure sheaf from generators of the algebra of the fibre product, and then deduces finite type, local quasi-finiteness and representability of the structure morphism before invoking the affine criterion for schemes. The presentation of the structure sheaf is the substance, so the claim is H2.
